Understanding Otosclerosis and Hearing Loss

Otosclerosis is a condition characterized by abnormal bone remodeling in the middle ear, specifically affecting the stapes bone. This prevents the bone from vibrating correctly, leading to progressive conductive hearing loss. Patients often describe a sensation of muffled sound or persistent tinnitus, which significantly impacts their quality of life.

How Microscopic Stapedotomy Restores Hearing

Microscopic Stapedotomy is a gold-standard surgical procedure designed to bypass the fixed stapes bone. Under high-powered magnification, Dr. Dhirendra Singh Kushwah performs this delicate surgery to create a small opening in the footplate of the stapes, inserting a tiny prosthesis to restore the transmission of sound vibrations to the inner ear.

Why Choose Dr. Dhirendra Singh Kushwah?

With over 25 years of experience, Dr. Kushwah combines surgical precision with the latest otological technology. Whether you are a local patient in Delhi-NCR or traveling from abroad, our clinics provide world-class care for complex ear conditions. If you are exploring options for Stapedotomy Surgery in Delhi NCR, our team ensures a personalized treatment plan aimed at optimal hearing recovery.

Benefits of the Procedure

  • Significant and often immediate improvement in hearing.
  • Minimally invasive, day-care or short-stay surgery.
  • High success rates in experienced hands.
  • Minimal recovery time compared to traditional methods.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Stapedotomy painful?

Most patients experience very little pain post-surgery. We utilize advanced anesthesia techniques to ensure patient comfort throughout the process.

How long is the recovery period?

While most patients return to light daily activities within a few days, we recommend avoiding strenuous exercise or heavy lifting for a few weeks to ensure proper healing.

Will my hearing be perfect immediately?

Hearing improvement is often noticeable shortly after the surgery, though it may take a few weeks for the middle ear to fully stabilize and for your hearing to reach its maximum potential.

Who is an ideal candidate for this surgery?

Candidates are typically those diagnosed with conductive hearing loss due to otosclerosis who have not seen sufficient results from hearing aids or prefer a permanent surgical solution.

title: Which ENT Issues Are Most Common in the Summer & How to Prevent Them
excerpt: Summer brings unique ear, nose, and throat challenges ranging from swimmer's ear to AC-induced sinusitis. Learn preventive tips from Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
Understanding Summer ENT Conditions

Summer in North India brings scorching temperatures, heavy air conditioning, and increased pool activities—all of which trigger unique ear, nose, and throat complications. Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah outlines the most common ENT conditions observed across his Delhi clinics:

1. Swimmer's Ear (Otitis Externa)

Water trapped in the external ear canal creates an ideal breeding ground for bacteria and fungi. Symptoms include sharp pain when pressing the ear tragus, redness, itching, and yellowish discharge. Prevention: Use silicone earplugs while swimming, tilt your head to drain trapped water, and never insert cotton swabs or sharp objects into the ear canal.

2. AC-Induced Sinusitis & Temperature Shock

Moving rapidly between 43°C outdoor heat and 21°C air-conditioned environments shocks the delicate nasal mucosa. The blood vessels constrict and dilate abruptly, causing swelling, nasal block, and mucus stasis leading to bacterial sinusitis.

3. Allergic Rhinitis & Dust Storms

Dry summer winds carry suspended particulate matter and allergens that irritate respiratory linings, resulting in repetitive sneezing, itchy palate, and runny nose. Saline nasal rinses and physician-prescribed antihistamines provide reliable relief.

title: Tympanoplasty & Eardrum Repair: Modern Microscopic & Endoscopic Techniques

Restoring Hearing and Protecting the Middle Ear

A perforated eardrum (tympanic membrane perforation) allows water and bacteria to penetrate the middle ear, leading to chronic discharge, foul odor, and progressive conductive hearing loss. Modern tympanoplasty reconstructs the sound-conducting mechanism with high graft uptake rates exceeding 95%.

Endoscopic vs Microscopic Ear Surgery

With high-definition Transcanal Endoscopic Ear Surgery (TEES), surgical repair is completed directly through the natural ear canal without any external incisions or stitches behind the ear. For complex ossicular chain reconstruction, surgical Carl Zeiss operating microscopes provide exceptional 3D depth perception.

Key Advantages of Modern Eardrum Repair

  • No External Scar: Performed completely through the ear canal in suitable cases.
  • Same-Day Discharge: Performed as a daycare procedure under local or short general anesthesia.
  • Hearing Restoration: Significant closure of the air-bone gap, returning clear natural hearing.

title: Chronic Sinusitis & FESS Surgery: Complete Guide to Long-Term Relief
excerpt: Persistent facial pressure, headache, and nasal congestion unresponsive to medicine? Learn how Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS) clears blocked sinuses.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
When Sinusitis Becomes Chronic

Sinusitis is diagnosed as chronic when inflammation of the paranasal sinuses persists for 12 weeks or longer despite medical therapy. Common symptoms include chronic facial pain, frontal headaches, thick nasal drip, loss of smell, and chronic fatigue.

How Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS) Works

FESS is a minimally invasive surgical procedure that restores natural ventilation and drainage to the sinus cavities. Using Karl Storz HD endoscopes and micro-debriders, Dr. Dhirendra Singh Kushwah widens obstructed sinus ostia and removes polyps with millimeter precision—without any external facial cuts or bruising.

Post-Operative Recovery

Modern sinus surgery avoids painful traditional nasal packing by utilizing dissolving biodegradable hemostatic spacers. Most patients return to desk work and light routine activities within 48 to 72 hours.

title: Snoring, Sleep Apnea & Coblation Tonsillectomy in Children & Adults
excerpt: Loud snoring, daytime drowsiness, and interrupted breathing during sleep indicate Obstructive Sleep Apnea. Learn about gentle Coblation plasma surgery.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
Quiet Nights and Restful Sleep

Loud snoring is more than an annoyance; it is often the cardinal sign of Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA). When throat muscles and enlarged tonsils or adenoids collapse into the airway, breathing repeatedly halts for 10 seconds or longer, causing dangerous drops in blood oxygen saturation.

The Role of Coblation Technology

Traditional tonsillectomy utilized electrocautery reaching temperatures of 400°C to 600°C, causing significant thermal injury and post-op throat pain. In contrast, Coblation (Controlled Ablation) utilizes radiofrequency energy in saline solution to generate a gentle plasma field operating at just 40°C to 70°C.

Benefits of Coblation Adenotonsillectomy:

  • Virtually zero intraoperative bleeding.
  • Dramatically reduced post-operative throat pain, allowing children to eat soft solid foods within hours.
  • Rapid recovery and resumption of school or work within days.

title: Pediatric Cochlear Implants: Early Detection & The Golden Window for Hearing
excerpt: For children born with severe-to-profound hearing loss, timely cochlear implantation before age 3 unlocks normal speech and language development.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
Unlocking the World of Sound for Deaf Children

When an infant is born with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss, conventional hearing aids cannot amplify sound adequately because the inner ear hair cells are damaged or absent. A Cochlear Implant bypasses the damaged cochlea, stimulating the auditory nerve directly through precision electrical pulses.

The Critical 'Golden Window' (0 to 3 Years)

The human brain possesses neuroplasticity for speech and language processing during the first few years of life. Children implanted before 2 to 3 years of age frequently attain speech clarity and language milestones on par with normal-hearing peers.

Key Early Signs Parents Must Watch For:

  • Infant does not startle or turn head toward loud claps or door slams by 6 months.
  • Child does not babble or respond to name by 10 to 12 months.
  • Failure to speak single words (Mama, Papa) by 18 months.

Our dedicated cochlear implant program includes pre-surgical high-resolution CT/MRI temporal bone evaluation, minimally invasive round-window insertion, and dedicated post-activation speech therapy.

title: Vertigo, Dizziness & BPPV: Diagnosis & Non-Surgical Treatment
excerpt: Feeling like the room is spinning when you turn in bed? Discover why Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) happens and how the Epley maneuver cures it.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
Why Does Vertigo Happen?

Vertigo is the sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning or tilting when there is no actual movement. More than 80% of vertigo cases originate inside the inner ear's vestibular balance system, rather than in the brain or neck.

Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

BPPV is the single most common inner ear disorder. Tiny microscopic calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) detach from their normal location in the utricle and become displaced into the fluid-filled semicircular canals. Turning your head or lying down shifts these crystals, creating abnormal fluid waves that confuse the brain with false motion signals.

Treatment with Canalith Repositioning (Epley Maneuver)

Medications like cinnarizine or betahistine provide only temporary symptomatic relief. The definitive cure for BPPV is the Epley Maneuver—a 10-minute series of gentle, guided head and body positions that roll the loose crystals safely out of the canal. Success rates exceed 90% in just one or two clinic sessions.

title: Packless Septoplasty: Modern, Painless Correction of Deviated Septum
excerpt: Struggling to breathe through one side of your nose? Discover how modern pack-less septoplasty straightens the deviated nasal septum without painful gauze packing.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
Breathe Freely Through Both Nostrils

A Deviated Nasal Septum (DNS) occurs when the central cartilage and bone separating your nasal passages is shifted off-center. This causes chronic one-sided or alternating nasal obstruction, recurrent sinus infections, mouth breathing, and morning dry throat.

The Fear of Traditional Nasal Packing

In older surgical practices, patients dreaded septoplasty because surgeons stuffed meters of vaseline-soaked gauze into both nostrils, forcing mouth breathing for 48 hours and causing intense pain upon removal.

Modern Pack-Less Technique by Dr. Kushwah

Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah performs Packless Septoplasty utilizing fine continuous quilt-suturing techniques and thin silicone splints with built-in airway channels. Benefits include:

  • Breathe naturally through your nose immediately after waking from anesthesia.
  • Virtually no pain, swelling, or facial black eyes.
  • Same-day or next-morning discharge with swift recovery.

title: Hoarseness of Voice & Vocal Cord Polyps: Advanced Micro-Laryngeal Care
excerpt: Are you a teacher, singer, or speaker experiencing persistent voice hoarseness? Learn how flexible laryngoscopy and micro-laryngeal surgery restore vocal clarity.
author: Dr. (Prof.) Dhirendra Singh Kushwah
content:
When Hoarseness Lasts More Than 2 Weeks

Voice change or hoarseness (dysphonia) that persists for more than two to three weeks should never be ignored. It often stems from benign vocal cord lesions caused by vocal overuse or acid reflux, but early specialist evaluation is vital to rule out early laryngeal malignancies, particularly in smokers.

Common Causes of Vocal Strain

  • Vocal Cord Nodules: Symmetrical callous-like growths on both vocal folds due to prolonged shouting or speaking.
  • Vocal Cord Polyps: Fluid-filled singular lesions, often arising after an acute episode of screaming or throat trauma.
  • Laryngopharyngeal Reflux (LPR): Stomach acid reaching the throat and burning vocal fold mucosa.

Minimally Invasive Micro-Laryngeal Surgery (MLS)

When conservative speech therapy and reflux medications do not resolve the lesion, Micro-Laryngeal Surgery is performed through the mouth under high magnification. The lesion is precisely excised without damaging the underlying delicate vocal ligament, restoring smooth phonation and voice stamina.
